official.description_text:
Tampere University
is
a unique, boldly future‑oriented and evolving community, and one of Finland’s most multidisciplinary universities. At Tampere University, technology, health and society come together in a distinctive way. Our research groups and projects carry out interdisciplinary and cross-sectoral research that transcends organisational boundaries. Our community is international, with members from more than 80 countries. Read more at
Tampere University (TAU) | Tampere University
.
HiPOVor
is an international doctoral network developing a new generation of high-power light beams carrying optical angular momentum. Fifteen doctoral researchers will work across the full technology chain, from beam generation and amplification to propagation, characterization and applications. The network brings together eight leading European universities and nine industrial partners, providing interdisciplinary training at the interface of advanced photonics, structured light and high-power laser technologies. The aim is to advance both fundamental science and practical applications, while training a new generation of specialists for academic and industrial careers.
Job description
Project title:
High power broadband fiber-based structured light with machine learning tuneable spatio-temporal characteristics
Project tasks and objectives
:  This doctoral project will explore how AI can control complex light inside multimode optical fibers. You will develop high-power broadband structured-light sources and use machine learning to tune their spatial, spectral and temporal properties on demand. The work combines nonlinear fiber optics, structured light, ultrafast photonics and AI, with the goal of turning complex multimode dynamics into a programmable light source rather than an uncontrolled effect.
Expected results
: The project will deliver new methods for AI-programmable all-fiber structured-light generation, enabling dynamically tunable beam shape, spectrum and temporal behavior at practical power levels. Potential applications include imaging, sensing, laser processing and industrial inspection.
Planned secondment(s)
: University of Warsaw (Poland), University of Stuttgart (Germany)
The Doctoral candidate will also be involved in dissemination through social media promotion of the network, such as project website, LinkedIn groups, YouTube video channels, and blogging.
Place of employment
: Tampere University, Finland
Supervisory team
: Professor Goëry Genty and Associate Professor Regina Gumenyuk
Expected starting date
: January 1st, 2027 at the latest.
Duration of the work contract
:  36 months
Trial period
: 6 months
Target degree
: PhD degree from Tampere University, Finland
Approximate gross salary
: The gross salary for the work contract in Finland is 3,950 euros/month (living allowance and mobility allowance).  If the fellow is eligible for family allowance, the salary for the work contract is approx. 4,450 euros/month. The salary will be defined in accordance with MSCA funding rules. The MSCA Fellow pays the Finnish progressive tax and employee unemployment insurance fee from the taxable monthly gross salary.
Requirements
We are looking for a talented, creative and highly motivated researcher with a strong background in photonics, optics, laser physics or a closely related field. Applicants are expected to have prior hands-on experience in experimental optics or photonics. Experience in nonlinear optics, optical fibes, ultrafast optics or structured light is particularly relevant. Skills in numerical modelling, Python/MATLAB, machine learning or optical data analysis are considered an advantage. The candidate should be comfortable with laboratory work and interested in combining advanced photonics experiments with computational and AI-based methods. The recruited researcher can be of any nationality, must be eligible for enrolment in the
doctoral programme at Tampere University
, must not hold a doctoral degree, and must fulfil the applicable employment requirements in Finland.
MSCA Mobility Rule
: at the time of recruitment by the host organization the researcher must not have resided or carried out his/her main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the country of his/her employer (Tampere University, Finland) for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately prior to his/her recruitment. Compulsory national service and/or short stays such as holidays and time spent as part of a procedure for obtaining refugee status under the Geneva Convention are not considered.
The applicant must be in possession of Master of Science (MSc) diploma.
English language requirements: Proficiency in written/spoken English is mandatory. In certain cases, we may ask for a language certificate.

How to apply
Please submit your application through our online recruitment system.
The closing date for applications is 21st of October 2026 (at 23:59 EEST / UTC +3).
The applicant must submit the following documents through LAURA recruitment system, only a clear copy of the documents will be considered.
Certified copies of the bachelor's and master's degree certificates with the Diploma Supplement (DS) as approved by the EU Commission for degrees completed in European universities (when applicable) Official translations into English (if the original documents are in a language other than English)
Curriculum Vitae/CV (preferably in
Europass
format)
List of publications (if any) your contributions in the publication
References: Contact details of 2 or more referees included in the CV
Motivation letter: maximum 1 page where you introduce yourself and present your qualifications; you may include also your previous research fields and main research results. Please emphasize your future goals career-wise
Please note that we will begin conducting interviews during the application period, so early applications are encouraged. This allows us to get to know candidates as soon as possible and keep the process moving efficiently. Please apply at your earliest convenience!
For more information, please contact:
Prof. Goëry Genty goery.genty@tuni.fi

Tampereen yliopisto
on ainutlaatuinen, rohkeasti tulevaisuuteen katsova, kehittyvä yhteisö ja yksi Suomen monialaisimmista yliopistoista. Meillä tekniikka, terveys ja yhteiskunta kohtaavat toisensa ainutlaatuisella tavalla. Tutkimusryhmissämme ja -hankkeissamme tehdään monitieteistä ja -alaista tutkimusta yli organisaatiorajojen. Yhteisömme on kansainvälinen, meitä on jo yli 80 maasta. Lue lisää
Tampereen yliopisto (TAU) | Tampereen yliopisto
.
Tehtävänkuvaus
Haemme väitöskirjatutkijaa hankkeeseen, jossa tutkitaan, miten tekoälyä ja koneoppimista voidaan hyödyntää monimuotokuiduissa etenevän monimutkaisen valon hallintaan. Tavoitteena on kehittää suuritehoisia ja laajakaistaisia rakenteisen valon kuitulähteitä, joiden avaruudellisia, spektraalisia ja ajallisia ominaisuuksia voidaan säätää dynaamisesti. Työ yhdistää epälineaarisen kuituoptiikan, rakenteisen valon, ultranopean fotoniikan ja tekoälyn. Tuloksena pyritään kehittämään uusia menetelmiä tekoälyohjattuun, täysin kuitupohjaiseen valon tuottamiseen, jossa säteen muotoa, spektriä ja ajallista käyttäytymistä voidaan ohjelmoida käytännöllisillä tehotasoilla. Mahdollisia sovelluksia ovat kuvantaminen, mittaus ja tunnistus, laserprosessointi sekä teollinen tarkastus.
Hakuohjeet
Lue tarkemmat tiedot tehtävästä ja hakuohjeet yllä olevasta englanninkielisestä ilmoituksesta. Jätäthän hakemuksesi yliopiston sähköisellä hakulomakkeella (linkki löytyy tämän ilmoituksen alta).
Hakuaika tehtävään päättyy 21.10.2026.

ai.summary: MSCA doctoral position in machine-learning-assisted structured light generation within multimode optical fibers at Tampere University. The work combines nonlinear fiber optics, AI/ML, and ultrafast photonics to develop programmable light sources with tunable spatial, spectral, and temporal properties for imaging, sensing, and industrial applications.

thematic_fit.rationale: No thematic alignment with human-centred XR, collaborative immersive systems, spatial learning, or wayfinding. The position is pure photonics and optical physics—outside the researcher's domain entirely.

methodological_fit.rationale: While both involve experimental work and data analysis, the methodologies are fundamentally different. This position emphasizes nonlinear fiber optics, ultrafast laser physics, and ML for signal/beam control—not HCI, user studies, or spatial-cognition evaluation. The researcher's experimental-design and quantitative-research skills are generic but insufficient given the specialized photonics substrate required.

growth_value.rationale: Python and ML experience would transfer, but the researcher would be starting from zero in photonics, optical physics, and laser engineering. No pathway to close gaps in spatial cognition, immersive design, or HCI—the core of their target identity. Growth would diverge sharply from target.

strategic_value.rationale: Tampere University is in a preferred country (Finland); MSCA funding is stable and prestigious. However, the supervisory team (Genty, Gumenyuk) are photonics specialists, not HCI or XR researchers. No strategic alignment with target institutional culture or research group ethos. Position offers European location but wrong disciplinary ecosystem.

eligibility_flags: Requires MSc in photonics, optics, laser physics or closely related field; researcher's MMU degree in Creative Multimedia does not satisfy 'closely related' criterion.
MSCA mobility rule: researcher must not have resided in Finland >12 months in prior 3 years; currently in Malaysia, so eligible.
Hands-on experimental optics/photonics required; researcher has no evidence of laboratory optics experience.
risks: Disciplinary mismatch is severe. Photonics/laser physics knowledge gap would require 6+ months remedial learning; likelihood of success is low.
Research supervisors are pure photonics specialists; no HCI or XR mentorship available. Risk of intellectual isolation relative to target identity.
Postdoctoral collaborator would focus on multimodal ML; still no human-centred research component.
Project endpoint (structured light sources, not human evaluation) does not build publication track record in HCI/XR venues.
Degree does not match stated requirement for 'strong background in photonics, optics, laser physics or closely related field'.
